questions.q: In the scenario, Load Interface File for Import succeeds cleanly before Import Payables Invoices rejects 13 of 200 rows. What does this tell the consultant?
options: The ZIP file itself must be corrupted
The entire batch must be rebuilt from scratch
The rejections are business-rule issues at the row level, not a file-structure problem, since the file already passed load-time validation
Nothing can be concluded from this information
questions.explain: Because load-time validation already succeeded, the consultant can rule out file-structure problems and focus on business-rule validation at the row level.

questions.q: Why does the consultant query AP_INVOICES_INTERFACE directly for the 9 'invalid supplier site' rejections instead of relying on the report alone?
options: Because the report is always wrong
Because the report doesn't show exactly which site code was entered, and the direct query reveals the specific value (a site code with a trailing space)
Because querying is required before every troubleshooting step regardless of need
Because UCM cannot produce reports
questions.explain: The execution report identified the error category but not the exact value; querying the interface table directly revealed the specific trailing-space mistake.

questions.q: What does the consultant do with the 187 rows that already succeeded?
options: Leave them completely untouched, since they are already live, correct records
Resubmit them along with the corrected rows, just to be safe
Delete them and re-enter them manually
Purge them immediately before fixing anything else
questions.explain: Following the discipline from lesson 21, successful rows are left alone — only the specific rejected rows are corrected and resubmitted.

questions.q: What is the correct cause of the 4 rejected rows with a header-to-line mismatch?
options: A UCM account that was selected incorrectly
An expired Oracle Fusion password
A macro security setting blocking CSV generation
The header invoice amount ($12,400.00) did not match the sum of the invoice's lines ($12,150.00)
questions.explain: This mirrors the header/line balancing validation from lesson 16 — the header total must equal the sum of its lines, or the row is rejected.

questions.q: In what order does the lesson recommend handling this entire scenario?
options: Purge the interface table first, then review the report
Resubmit the entire original file immediately without reading any report
Trust the clean load-time result, read the execution report, query interface tables if needed, fix and resubmit only the failed rows, and purge only after confirming success
Delete all 200 rows and start over from a blank template
questions.explain: This is the reusable five-step order the lesson teaches: trust the clean load, read the report, query when needed, fix narrowly, and purge only after confirming the fix worked.
